title: Expanding binomial products
log: 2026-11-04T09:36:56Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The bank point covers factorising and special expansions such as perfect squares and difference of two squares, not the general expansion of a binomial product like (x + 3)(x + 5), so it is related but broader and does not teach the same idea.

draft.title: Expanding binomial products
card: A binomial is an expression with two terms, such as x + 3. To expand a product of two binomials, multiply each term in the first bracket by each term in the second.
Worked example: (x + 3)(x + 5) = x × x + x × 5 + 3 × x + 3 × 5 = x² + 5x + 3x + 15.
Then collect like terms. 5x + 3x = 8x, so the answer is x² + 8x + 15.
Take care with signs. A negative term makes negative products, so (x − 2)(x + 4) = x² + 4x − 2x − 8 = x² + 2x − 8.
draft.remember: Every term in the first bracket meets every term in the second. Then collect like terms.

a.why: x × x = x², x × 7 = 7x, 2 × x = 2x and 2 × 7 = 14. Then 7x + 2x = 9x. Giving x² + 14 skips the two middle products.
a.clue: Make four products, then add the two x terms.

b.why: The products are x², 6x, −3x and −18. Then 6x − 3x = 3x, giving x² + 3x − 18. Adding 6x and 3x instead ignores the negative sign on the 3.
b.clue: The 3 in the first bracket is being taken away.
